## Pitch

**Working title:** When “Ultra” Thinking Makes an LLM Worse

As an AI engineer or technical leader tuning a reasoning model, I want to understand why maximum reasoning effort can reduce benchmark and agent performance, so that I can benchmark the cost/accuracy curve for my own workloads rather than treating more thinking tokens as automatically better.

The story will explain **overthinking** as the umbrella failure mode: an o1-style model spends excessive test-time compute on a task, producing no gain or an accuracy decline. It will distinguish that from **inverse scaling with test-time compute**, the specific non-monotonic pattern where additional reasoning tokens hurt measured accuracy.

## Reader stake

“Ultra” is a cost and reliability setting, not a quality guarantee. The practical close should be a lightweight evaluation plan: test representative workloads at each reasoning level; record accuracy, latency, token cost, and failure modes; then choose the smallest budget that meets the operational target.

## Evidence to verify and use

- Chen et al., “Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs” (Dec. 2024): https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.21187
- “Do LLMs Overthink Basic Math Reasoning? Benchmarking the ...”: https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1285.pdf
- “Examining the Reasoning-Action Dilemma in Agentic Tasks”: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.08235.pdf
- “Declining Legal Classification Performance in Reasoning LLMs”: https://www.cs.cit.tum.de/fileadmin/w00cfj/sebis/_my_direct_uploads/Wa26b.pdf
- Apple, “The Illusion of Thinking” — verify the precise findings and preferred primary citation before drafting.

Use primary research and original benchmark results only for claims. Treat reported figures—including 18× tokens, the 7.9% issue-resolution relationship, and o1-high vs. o1-low SWE-bench performance—as leads that require source-level verification before publication.

## Anth.us angle

Frame thinking effort as an MLOps control: measure quality, token spend, latency, and agent interaction with environmental feedback. The useful outcome is an operating policy for production-scale agentic AI, not a generic warning against reasoning models.

## Scope

- Explain the terminology and evidence without implying that all longer reasoning is harmful.
- Cover simple benchmarks and agentic tasks separately.
- Give concrete evaluation checks for model operators.
- Do not make unverified model-performance or cost claims.

## Acceptance criteria

Feature: Calibrating reasoning effort

Scenario: A reader chooses a reasoning budget
Given a team is configuring a reasoning model for a production workload
When it evaluates representative tasks at low, medium, high, and maximum reasoning settings
Then it can identify whether extra test-time compute improves, plateaus, or harms quality
And it can select a budget using accuracy, latency, token cost, and environmental-feedback outcomes.
